_om: Engelsk översättning av texter.json. Bara texter; siffrorna står i den svenska filen. horn och riktningar sätts in efter "the" eller "to the", regioner i "the {region} part of the tower".

1: The gate is a tall, vaulted opening in the wall. The threshold is worn smooth by all who went in before you. The air inside is warmer than the evening outside.
You stand inside the gate. The daylight reaches only a few steps in, then gives up. The stone underfoot is strangely soft at the edges.
2: The edges of the gate are softer than before, and the threshold is damp.
Outside, the light falls aslant. The gate seems a little smaller than when you came.
3: The arch of the gate has teeth: small, backward-curving teeth in a row along the edge, so that it is easy to go in and hard to go out.
On the threshold lies a boot. The foot is still in it.
4: The gate is a mouth. It has stood open all day, and now it is beginning to close.
The lips draw together. The light outside has become a thin sliver. Run.

1: The hall is round and sinks towards the middle. There, gold glimmers in a heap, and around the heap lies something vast in heavy, slow coils. It is too dark to see where it begins or ends.
The air is still and thick with sweetness. Coins, crowns and dented goblets lie in a heap. Something large rests around it. You hear it breathe.
2: The heap of gold rises and falls, like something breathing. The coils around it are not quite still.
Something breathes in here, but the breaths do not come from the coils. They come from the walls.
3: The walls are folded and glistening. Among the coins lie swords, shields, helmets and bones, all of them glossy and half dissolved.
The coils around the heap are not a sleeping serpent. They are folds in the wall, and they move when the wall moves.
4: This is the stomach. The treasure is what the serpent has swallowed: gold, armour and everyone who came to take it.
There is no serpent in the chamber. The chamber is in the serpent. The gold is the bait, and you have taken it.

rumstyper.kort: a narrow passage under low vaults

1: A narrow passage under low vaults. The stone is damp and faintly warm against your palm.
The vaults stand close, arch after arch, as if built to hold against a pressure from outside.
2: The vaults rise and fall almost imperceptibly, at the same slow pace as your own breathing. Though not quite the same.
You lay your hand against the wall. It is warm, and beneath the surface runs a faint, steady motion, like waves.
3: The vaults are not masonry. They are curved white arches that meet up in the ceiling, close after one another. Like ribs.
Between two arches a helmet is wedged fast, and in it the remains of a face, glossy and half dissolved.
4: These are no vaults. They are ribs, and you are walking through the chest of something alive. It breathes around you.
The arches tighten as it breathes in. You are inside it. You have been all along.

1: Thick pillars stand in two rows. Between them hangs a sweet, heavy scent you cannot place.
The pillars are coarse and lean slightly inwards, all in the same direction.
2: The pillars swell a little and draw in again. The sweet scent comes in gusts, like breath.
The floor between the pillars is damp and lukewarm. It sways, barely noticeably, underfoot.
3: The pillars are not stone. They are tough, pale strands stretched between floor and ceiling, and they tighten as you pass.
By a pillar lies a pack. The straps have dissolved, and what was inside has become a yellow slime.
4: The pillars are sinews. The whole hall is a muscle, and it has begun to contract.
The scent is digestion. You understand now what it is that smells sweet here, and why.

rumstyper.kort: a room with a bottomless well

1: A well with no visible bottom in the middle of the floor. Far below, water drips, at long intervals.
The rim of the well is polished smooth. From the depths rises a lukewarm, damp air.
2: The water in the well rises and sinks at a slow pace, as if something breathes down there.
The dripping from the depths has found a rhythm. Thud, thud. It no longer sounds like water.
3: The rim of the well is round and soft, with folds like a gullet. A sour smell rises from the depths.
Far down in the well a hand is floating. It has no skin left, but the ring is still on its finger.
4: The well is a gullet, and it leads downwards, towards the stomach. What falls in never comes up.
What you heard dripping was saliva. The sound from the depths is swallowing.

rumstyper.kort: a room with an overturned bench and a rusty spear

1: An overturned bench and a rusty spear. Whoever kept watch here left in great haste.
Someone has carved a single sentence into the door frame: WE WERE WRONG ABOUT THE WAY IN. The rest is scraped away.
2: The spear that lay on the floor has moved. The floor now slopes the other way.
The sentence in the door frame is clearer now. Someone has written more beneath it: IT MOVES.
3: The guards' beds have grown fast into the wall. The wall has grown around them, slowly, like bark around a nail.
Under the bench lies a guard, or what is left of one. The bones are glossy and soft at the edges, as if something has sucked on them.
4: The guards were not here to keep people out. They were trying to keep themselves alive, inside it.
WE WERE WRONG ABOUT THE WAY IN, it said. Now you understand: the way in was a mouth.

1: A small chapel without images. The floor tiles are worn in a pattern of small, overlapping shields.
The pews face away from the altar, towards the wall. No one knows why.
2: The shield pattern in the floor glistens, as if it were wet. The tiles lie closer than before.
It is quiet in the chapel, but the quiet beats. A dull, steady beat, somewhere beneath the floor.
3: The floor tiles are scales. Real scales, large as shields, and beneath them something warm is pulsing.
Someone has carved a prayer into the wall. It ends in the middle of a word, and the carving is half grown over.
4: No one has prayed here. The chapel is a fold of skin, and the pews face the wall because the flesh was once thinnest there.
Beneath the scales the heart is beating. You stand closer to it than any human should.

rumstyper.kort: a hall with a stair that ends at the ceiling

1: A staircase winds upwards and ends flat against the ceiling. The steps are of uneven height.
The stair twists around a thick central pillar. It leads nowhere.
2: The stair twists slowly, perhaps only half a step, and then twists back.
The steps are warm. They are joined by something tough, like gristle.
3: Every step is a vertebra. You see the hole in the middle of each one, where something thick runs upwards.
Halfway up, an adventurer is stuck fast in the central pillar, embedded to the waist. They do not move.
4: The stair is a spine. It runs through the whole tower, and it leads nowhere because it was never a way.
The spine bends. The whole tower bends, like a serpent making ready.

rumstyper.kort: a room of shelves, jugs and barrels

1: Shelves of jugs and barrels. Everything is covered in a thin, glossy film, as of damp that never dries.
Sacks that once held grain. Now they are empty and sticky on the inside.
2: The film on the barrels moves when you breathe, as if it breathes with you.
The sticky stuff in the sacks is warm. There is more of it than a moment ago.
3: The jugs are not made of clay. They are glossy, hollow bones, and in them lie the remains of something that was once food.
Among the sacks lies a cloak. Of whoever wore it, not much is left: buckles, buttons, a tooth.
4: This is no storeroom. It is where it keeps what it has not yet had time to digest. You are one of those things too.
The film is stomach juice. It has lain on everything in here, and now it lies on you.

rumstyper.kort: a hall with iron hooks in the ceiling

1: Iron hooks in the ceiling where lanterns once hung. Your own flame flickers in a draught that comes and goes, comes and goes.
Soot on the walls in long streaks. Someone once tried to smoke something out of here.
2: The draught comes and goes, comes and goes. It is no draught. It is breath.
The flame bends inwards and then outwards, at a steady pace, as if the room breathes through a single nostril.
3: The hooks in the ceiling are not iron. They are curved, yellow-white spikes pointing inwards.
The streaks of soot on the wall are finger marks. Someone clawed at the wall here, for a long time.
4: The hooks are teeth, and the lantern hall is the palate. Whoever tried to smoke something out of here understood too late where they were.
The breaths come from the lungs just behind the wall. Each time the flame bends, it breathes.

rumstyper.kort: a cave with smooth, white-striped walls

1: The walls here are not built but smooth, almost polished. White stripes run along them in even arcs.
The room is more cave than hall. The stone has a faint pattern, as of fine squares.
2: The white stripes run in arcs that tighten and relax.
The fine pattern of squares in the stone glimmers faintly in your light, like scales in water.
3: The pattern of squares is scales, seen from inside. You stand in a skin, between two layers of the same body.
On the floor lies a shed skin, and inside it a skeleton in armour, curled up like an unborn child.
4: The cave is the skin seen from the inside. Everything smooth here has been worn down by what has moved past for a hundred years.
The white is scars: old wounds left by those who tried to cut their way out.

rumstyper.kort: a room with an anvil and a dead hearth

1: An anvil and a dead hearth. Even so, it is warmer here than it should be.
The tools hang neatly on the wall. All of them are bent, as if they have been squeezed.
2: The warmth does not come from the hearth. It comes from the walls, in gusts.
The bent tools have bent a little further.
3: The wall behind the hearth has an edge of dissolved iron, as if it has been eating a spade.
In the hearth lie ashes and teeth. Human teeth.
4: What squeezed the tools was muscle. The forge is part of the gut, and the gut is pressing.
The warmth is body heat. You have been walking about inside a warm-blooded beast.

rumstyper.kort: a room full of swollen grey books

1: The books have swollen together into a grey mass. Someone has scratched lines in the wall. Many lines.
A book lies open. The pages are stuck together by something sweet.
2: The grey mass of books swells and sinks slowly. The pages rustle, as if someone were breathing on them.
There are more lines in the wall now. You start to count them. It takes too long.
3: The lines are days. Whoever scratched them lived here, inside it, for months.
A hand is stuck in the mass of books, melted together with the pages. It is holding a pen.
4: On the last legible page it says: the tower is no building. It is a body, and we are what it eats.
Whoever scratched the lines did not stop because they got out.

rumstyper.kort: a place where the walls meet in a pointed arch

1: The walls meet in a pointed arch. A distant sound, as of something heavy shifting, dies away before you can listen.
Here the passages cross. The floor slopes faintly to the {horn}.
2: The floor slopes to the {horn}, and the slope has grown steeper.
The sound of something heavy shifting comes back, and now you hear that it comes from every side.
3: The passages meet here like blood vessels, and the walls are full of thin pipes that pulse.
In the crossing lie three knucklebones in a heap, arranged as a warning. No one has understood it.
4: All the passages lead towards the stomach. That was why the floor sloped. You have been led there, step by step.
The sound of something heavy shifting was you. You are what shifts inside it.
